# pistol golden games, v1 — the turn-structure oracle for game rules 3 and 4.
#
# Pinned by SHA-256 in crates/pistol-core/tests/golden_game_tests.rs
# (GOLDEN_GAMES_SHA256). docs/decisions.md D-12 promises that the sha-pinned
# goldens cover the first-stone-win truncation and the second-stone win. A board
# without a move list cannot express either — both are statements about WHEN a
# stone was played, not about where the stones ended up — so those cases live
# here, pinned, rather than in a Rust array that can drift without anyone
# noticing (D-43).
#
# Format. One block per case; `plies` accumulates, `expect` is given once:
#
#   case <name>
#   plies <q,r> <q,r> ...            stones in play order, repeatable
#   expect ongoing turn <n> phase <first|second>
#                                    after the last ply: whose turn it is and
#                                    how far into it
#   expect win <p1|p2> on-turn <n> as <first|second>-stone
#                                    the last ply completed a run of six or
#                                    more: who won, the turn it was scored on,
#                                    and whether it was that turn's first stone
#                                    — in which case the second is never played
#                                    — or its second
#
# Turn 1 is one stone and every later turn is two, so a ply list groups as
# 1, 2, 2, 2, … and the turn each ply belongs to is fixed by its position. The
# comments mark the turns; they are commentary, and the loader ignores them.
#
# Every game here is legal all the way through: every stone lands within
# hex-distance 8 of a stone already on the board, the first on the origin, and
# no side completes a run before the case says so.

case p1_wins_on_the_first_stone_of_its_turn
plies 0,0
plies 0,2 2,2
plies 1,0 2,0
plies 4,2 6,2
plies 3,0 4,0
plies 0,4 2,4
plies 5,0
expect win p1 on-turn 7 as first-stone

case p1_wins_on_the_second_stone_of_its_turn
plies 0,0
plies 0,2 2,2
plies 1,0 0,3
plies 4,2 6,2
plies 2,0 3,0
plies 0,4 2,4
plies 4,0 5,0
expect win p1 on-turn 7 as second-stone

case p2_wins_on_the_second_stone_of_its_turn
plies 0,0
plies 0,2 1,2
plies 0,5 2,5
plies 2,2 3,2
plies 4,5 6,5
plies 4,2 5,2
expect win p2 on-turn 6 as second-stone

case five_in_a_row_leaves_the_game_ongoing
plies 0,0
plies 0,2 2,2
plies 1,0 2,0
plies 4,2 6,2
plies 3,0 4,0
plies 0,4 2,4
expect ongoing turn 7 phase first

case five_in_a_row_mid_turn_leaves_the_game_ongoing
plies 0,0
plies 0,2 2,2
plies 1,0 0,3
plies 4,2 6,2
plies 2,0 3,0
plies 0,4 2,4
plies 4,0
expect ongoing turn 7 phase second
